items.text:
• 𝗛𝗦𝗖𝗧 𝗱𝗼𝗻𝗼𝗿 𝘀𝗲𝗹𝗲𝗰𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻
Turner et al. - HLA-DPB1 TCE mismatch vector differentially affects HCT outcomes in 10/10 and ≤9/10 HLA matched patients in the UK. Transplantation and Cellular Therapy, 2026.
Online: 18 Sep 2026.

Among 1,743 unrelated-donor transplants, DPB1 mismatch direction distinguished outcome associations within T-cell epitope groups: host-versus-graft mismatches were associated with better survival in ≤9/10 pairs. This could refine donor selection, but the retrospective 1996–2020 cohort requires validation in contemporary practice.

https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jtct.2026.09.033

• 𝗣𝗼𝗽𝘂𝗹𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻 𝗱𝗶𝘃𝗲𝗿𝘀𝗶𝘁𝘆 & 𝗛𝗟𝗔 𝗿𝗲𝗳𝗲𝗿𝗲𝗻𝗰𝗲 𝗱𝗮𝘁𝗮
da Silva et al. - GERBase: an online tool for high-resolution HLA allele and haplotype frequencies and linkage disequilibrium analysis in a Brazilian population. Frontiers in Genetics, 2026;17:1973772.
Online: 14 Oct 2026.

An open resource provides 17,260 family-phased haplotypes; 9,026 span all nine classical loci. Directly observed haplotypes support laboratory plausibility checks and population-aware donor searches, but this transplant-candidate cohort is not a nationally representative reference.

https://doi.org/10.3389/fgene.2026.1973772

From our Journal HLA Immune Response Genetics:
• 𝗔𝗻𝘁𝗶𝗯𝗼𝗱𝘆 𝗲𝗽𝗶𝘁𝗼𝗽𝗲𝘀 & 𝗮𝘀𝘀𝗮𝘆 𝗶𝗻𝘁𝗲𝗿𝗽𝗿𝗲𝘁𝗮𝘁𝗶𝗼𝗻
Meng et al. - Concentration-Dependent Reactivity Profiles of a Human Monoclonal Antibody Recognising HLA-DQB1*04/05/06 and at Reduced Intensities to DQB1*03 Antigens. HLA, 2026;108:e70889.
Online: 21 Oct 2026.

Engineered HLA-DQ variants supported contributions from residues 46V and 55R, while higher antibody concentrations revealed weaker reactivity, including to self antigens. A useful challenge for epitope assignment and bead-assay interpretation; evidence comes from one monoclonal antibody, with clinical significance unresolved.

https://doi.org/10.1111/tan.70889
